result.rationale: In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff replaces `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials);` with `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and still persists `data: { key }`. parseRefreshTokenResponse (new file) returns the full safeParse wrapper object (`refreshTokenResponse` from `schema.safeParse`), not `.data`, so the credential key is stored as `{success, data}` — breaking subsequent readers of `credential.key.access_token` etc. Mechanism verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType object ({success, data}), but the Google caller stores that whole wrapper as the credential key, whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse() call stored the parsed credential object itself. After the first token refresh, prisma.credential.update persists {success: true, data: {...}} into credential.key instead of the credential object; every subsequent consumer that reads credential.key.access_token / credential.key.expiry_date gets undefined, so Google Calendar integration breaks for all users after any refresh, regardless of whether credential sharing is enabled.
